reviewer: claude-fable-5 acting as the joshi callout-science deputy, autonomously, without Ember present
rationale: AMENDED v2, 2026-08-23, on top of the v1 review of 2026-08-22 (7 bodies, 61 rows, promoted; its full findings stand: createdAt/peakTimestamp are epoch-millisecond OCCURRENCE times with no availability instant anywhere; multiple/maxPriceSol/peakTimestamp are outcomes as of the read; calloutPrice and maxPriceSol are recomputed at read time against the current SOL price and this route exposes no USD twins; the required set is the ten leaves the projection reads). THE AMENDMENT: `$/peakTimestamp:number` moves from required to optional. REVIEWED MATERIAL: an 80-mint sweep on 2026-08-23 (retained bodies, callout-science state), in which 41 bodies promoted with 907 rows, 33 answered the empty page {"callouts":[]} (correctly refused as row-uncheckable and retained as absent records), and 6 bodies were refused solely because at least one row OMITS peakTimestamp entirely - not null, absent. Every other leaf on every row of all 6 bodies is in the reviewed sets, and multiple and maxPriceSol are present on those rows. An absent peakTimestamp is the no-peak-yet state (the sibling route encodes the same state as maxMultiplierAt:null); a callout that has never exceeded its callout price has no peak instant to report. Requiring the leaf therefore refuses exactly the youngest and the never-peaked callouts, which is the survivorship error this project keeps catching: the =1 floor rows are the failed calls, and a gate that drops them silently curates the corpus toward winners. The reader now must handle absence explicitly as no-peak-as-of-read, never as missing data. Nothing else changed; the optional set remains closed and lists only observed leaf lines. This amendment was made by an agent, not by Ember.
